So the parts were complete enough to weigh and measure: the failure is regional breakage and deformation, not a missing part (it could also be filed as partly_failed). Mechanism in the authors' words (Sect. 4.4 bullet): 'the curvature radius of the structure decreases, reducing self-supporting effects. As a result, certain regions lack sufficient mechanical stability during the printing process, leading to deformation or failure'. The abstract says 'the decreased curvature radius'. That is geometrically inverted, since a larger cell has larger radii; 'lower curvature' is an interpretation, not the paper's wording. Bridge/ledge rule: in Fig. 9 only 80%/20 mm lies purely above the 'not self supporting' line ('Local deformation'). 90%/20 mm also lies right of the 'sheet thickness < manufacturing limit' line and is marked 'Incomplete/fragile', so it is a mixed case. 70%/20 mm (t = 1.960 mm) is also 'Local deformation' in Fig. 9 and appears in Fig. 7, where Sect. 4.3 reports 'noticeable deviations and larger surface defects'. Layer thickness, scan speed and the laser power actually used are not stated; 200 W is the system's laser. case.source_title: Towards experimental process parameter development for Ti-6Al-4V TPMS lattice structures with application to small scale dental implants using micrographs
case.authors_year: Jahn A., Li H., Emminghaus N., Melnyk T., Hermsdorf J., Kaierle S., 2023, Proc. 34th Annual International Solid Freeform Fabrication Symposium (SFF 2023), pp. 2088–2100
case.material: Ti-6Al-4V Grade 23 (ECKART TLS GmbH, particle size 20.0–53.0 µm)
case.machine: DMG MORI Lasertec 12 SLM (400 W fibre laser, 1070 nm, continuous wave, minimum spot diameter 35 µm)
case.cell_mm: 1.0 and 1.8 (0.1 mm walls); 1.4 and 2.2 (0.3 mm walls)
case.volume_fraction: Design overall porosity (Table 1): 70% (1.0 mm cell / 0.1 mm wall), 83% (1.8 / 0.1), 38% (1.4 / 0.3), 59% (2.2 / 0.3)
case.orientation: Not stated in the text. The figures show it: Fig. 3 (build job layout) has the 7 × 7 × 7 mm³ cubes standing upright, 1 mm solid base at the bottom, raised on support structures drawn in orange. The Table 1 renderings show the cell axes parallel to the cube edges, so one cell axis stands along the build direction.
case.outcome_words: "Small structures with unit cell size as small as 1.0 mm are fabricated on a laser powder bed fusion industrial machine."
case.where: Abstract; Design of experiments (text and Table 1); Results and Discussion, 'Preliminary results of the DOE modeling', Table 6 (all 16 run-1 parts); Tables 3–4 (CT of parts 10, 11, 14, 15); Fig. 3 (build layout)
case.notes:
This is the thinnest designed wall fabricated in this source. The source does NOT report as-built wall thickness or geometric accuracy. Conclusions: the manufactured volume fraction 'is not completely analyzed yet and will be discussed in a later work'. So the case shows that 0.1 mm-designed sheets were fabricated with no failure reported. It does not show that they came out 0.1 mm thick.

DOE and measurements:
- Design: 2^4 factorial, 16 experiments, 2 runs. Laser 70/135 W, scan speed 800/1000 mm/s (Table 2), hatch 0.085 mm.
- The 16 specimens of the first run were sectioned, with 4 micrograph layers each.
- Table 6 internal porosity: 0.33–2.39% for the 0.1 mm walls (parts 5–12) and 0.34–5.62% for the 0.3 mm walls.
- Parts 10 and 11 (0.1 mm wall, 1.8 mm cell) were also CT-scanned: 1.59% and 1.27% (Table 3).
- The text mentions 'high surface roughness' for low-volume-fraction, thin-walled parts.

Design choices:
- The 0.1 mm wall was chosen because 'a minimal feature size lies at about 70 µm' with this spot.
- Designed pores are 0.4 and 0.8 mm.
- The base has 0.4 mm holes 'for better powder removal'. Cleaning was ultrasonic in isopropanol. Powder removal was not evaluated.
- The micrograph method notes 'sintered-on powder can be found inside pores'.

Pre-study (Fig. 1, a photo of cylinders): gyroid and diamond, UC 1 or 2 mm, wall 0.15 or 0.35 mm, high and low energy density. The text says 'With the same process parameter, some TPMS designs can be manufactured while others cannot be built' but does not say which.

Any comparison with a fixed 0.25 mm minimum from other cases is our inference, not the source's. It stays weak while the as-built wall is unknown.

Second Ti-6Al-4V success, checked: Bobbert et al. 2017, Acta Biomater 53:572–584, doi:10.1016/j.actbio.2017.02.024, TU Delft green OA copy.
- 1.5 mm unit cells; P/I-WP/G/D sheets.
- Designed sheet thickness 0.155–0.381 mm.
- Micro-CT sheet thickness 0.244–0.444 mm 'from top' and 0.246–0.442 mm 'from side' (Table 2).
- Ti6Al4V Grade 23 ELI 'built on support structures with a customized version of the 3D Systems ProX DMP 320'.
- 'the laser processing parameters had to be optimized for every porosity of every type of minimal surface'.

kept.why: The BAM OPUS link served a bot-check page to scripts. I read the full text from PubMed Central (PMC8198966, Europe PMC JATS XML) and the PMC figure images. Crossref confirms Materials 14(11):3002, 2021. These match the source: ARCAM A2, Ti-6Al-4V powder bought from ARCAM, 50 µm layers, 720 °C, Melt Theme, and Wafer Theme for the FGPS (Sect. 2.1). The structures are sheet-based gyroid (Abstract, Introduction). The design is k = 2, and k(z) = 1 + jz with j = 0.05, with no units on x, y, z, so there is no cell size in mm. Cubes: WT 0.4 and 0.6 mm, 15 mm, 'relative material apparent density of 50% and 42%, respectively'. FGPS: a zero-thickness model, plus a comparison model of nominal WT 0.25 mm (Sect. 3.5). Cleaning: PRS for 10 min; HF/HNO3 etching. The outcome quote is word for word in Sect. 3.5. Fig. 13 marks '1.64 mm' at a dotted line on the mean pore-size curve and carries the label 'BD=Gradient direction'. Its powder volume fraction is zero on the larger-pore side and rises on the smaller-pore side, which confirms the case's reading. Fig. 3 shows retained powder in 2 × 04 after PRS. The CE quote (Sect. 3.3), 'stalactite-like' (Sect. 3.2) and 'up to 30% thicker' (Conclusions) are word for word. Corrections: (1) Fig. 1 does not show the cubes' orientation; only Fig. 1c has a BD arrow. Fig. 6 labels the cube axes 'BD/Z', and Sect. 3.2 proposes a 45° tilt as a remedy, so the cubes stood with a cell axis along BD. (2) The readable copy is now PMC. (3) Added the as-built WT figures stated in Sects. 3.2–3.3. Caveat: the cell size in mm is stated nowhere, so only the measured pore (channel) size can be tested against rules.

case.source_title: X-ray Computed Tomography Procedures to Quantitatively Characterize the Morphological Features of Triply Periodic Minimal Surface Structures
case.authors_year: Evsevleev S., Mishurova T., Khrapov D., Paveleva A., Meinel D., Surmenev R., Surmeneva M., Koptyug A., Bruno G., 2021, Materials 14(11):3002
case.material: Ti-6Al-4V (precursor powder purchased from ARCAM EBM)
case.machine: ARCAM A2 EBM, process temperature 720 °C; standard ARCAM 'Melt Theme' for the constant-porosity cubes, standard 'Wafer Theme' for the graded specimen
case.lattice_as_named: sheet-based gyroid TPMSS: constant-porosity cubes '2 × 04' and '2 × 06' (15 × 15 × 15 mm) and a gyroid-based functionally graded porous scaffold (FGPS)
case.cell_mm: Not stated in mm. The source gives only sin(kx)cos(ky)+sin(ky)cos(kz)+sin(kz)cos(kx)=0, with k = 2 for the cubes and k(z) = 1 + 0.05z for the FGPS. Units of x, y, z are not given.
case.wall_mm: Cubes: 0.4 and 0.6 nominal. As-built 2 × 06 mean WT is 'around 470 µm' (Sect. 3.3). In 2 × 06, vertical walls are 'up to 180 µm (around 30%) thinner than the nominal WT' (Sect. 3.2). FGPS: zero-thickness model, so the wall is set by the 'Wafer Theme' beam strategy and no number is given. It was compared with a model of nominal WT 0.25.
case.volume_fraction: Cubes: 'relative material apparent density of 50% and 42%, respectively' for WT 0.4 and 0.6, in the order stated. FGPS: not stated.
case.orientation: Cubes: Fig. 6 labels the cube axes 'BD/Z', i.e. the cube Z axis is the build direction. Sect. 3.2 proposes building cubic TPMSS 'tilted by 45°' as a remedy. So the cubes were built with a cell axis along BD; Fig. 1a,b carry no BD arrow. FGPS: the porosity gradient runs along the build direction (Sect. 3.5 text; Fig. 12c BD arrow; Fig. 13 'BD=Gradient direction').
case.outcome_words: "the efficiency of the powder removal process is only satisfactory for pore sizes up to 1.6 mm. Lower porosity leads to the presence of RP"
case.where: Sect. 3.5 and Figs. 12–13 (FGPS; '1.64 mm' marked on the mean pore-size curve); Sect. 3.1 / Fig. 3 (2 × 04 after PRS, retained powder); Sect. 3.3 / Fig. 9 (both cubes after CE); Sect. 2.1 (design, machine, cleaning)
case.notes:
Test case for the channel rule. The threshold is a CT-measured pore size, not a cell size. No cell size in mm is stated, so only the pore-size number can be used.

Fig. 13 plots mean, max and CAD pore size and the volume fraction of entrapped powder (VFpowder) against distance from the bottom. A dotted line marks '1.64 mm' on the mean curve. VFpowder is zero on the larger-pore side below that line and rises on the smaller-pore side above it. So pores smaller than about 1.6 mm (mean) kept powder; the text's 'up to 1.6 mm' is worded the other way round.

Cleaning:
- All specimens: standard ARCAM Powder Recovery System for 10 min.
- One cube per WT was also chemically etched (1% HF : 10% HNO3).
- 'In both 2 × 04 and 2 × 06 specimens, the CE could not completely remove the RP from the structure.' Powder remained in the centre, at around 5 mm (2 × 06) and 6 mm (2 × 04) from the edges (Sect. 3.3).
- PRS efficiency 'drops with the distance from the specimen's outer surface, leaving the powder residue mainly in the center of the specimen' (Sect. 3.1).
- EBM residual powder is 'semi-sintered'.

Horizontal walls: liquid metal can 'leak' through the powder bed, giving 'excessive surface roughness and even stalactite-like structures' (Sect. 3.2). Horizontal walls 'appear up to 30% thicker than the vertical ones' (Conclusions).

As stated, the source gives the thicker 0.6 mm wall the lower density (42%).

Readable copy: https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC8198966/ (CC BY 4.0). The BAM OPUS file https://opus4.kobv.de/opus4-bam/files/52814/materials_final.pdf served a bot-check page to scripts.

kept.why: Read the full 9-page Lirias PDF. It is Elsevier's uncorrected proof, watermarked 'UNCORRECTED PROOF'. Crossref confirms J. Mater. Process. Technol. 275:116367, 2020. These match the source: Concept Laser M-lab cusing, 100 W fibre laser, 50 µm spot; 316L from Praxair, D50 31 µm; 90 W, 600 mm/s, 0.077 mm hatch, 30 µm layers (Sect. 2.2). Cells are a = 4 mm, five per axis, in 20 mm cubes. RD is 15%, or 20%→10% with G1 along the build direction and G2 along Y (Sect. 2.1, Fig. 1). Table 1 gives mean RD 16.33/15.91/16.34%. On raw UCS, 5-10 is higher (0.43 ± 0.13 vs 0.24 ± 0.04 MPa, SI Table S6). (2) SI Table S5 gives the 5-10 wall as 131 ± 3 µm (main text: 132 ± 3) and the 5-15 wall as 236 ± 7 µm. (3) SI Tables S5 and S6 show 5-20 as a dash, captioned 'Dashes indicate print failures', so nothing was measured. (4) I added the Fig. 1a legend and the Sec. 3.6 rule. (5) I reworded the 200 µm skin point to what Sec. 2.2 literally says.

case.source_title: Partially decoupling cell size and density as tailorable design parameters in mSLA-printed gyroid cores for sustainable sandwich panels
case.authors_year: Luthuli, Schlesinger, Christodoulides, Vos, Gabriel, Dicks (2026, Research Square preprint v1, posted 12 Nov 2026)
case.material: eSun eResin-PLA Pro transparent (partially biobased PLA-based polyurethane acrylate photopolymer, PLA-PUA)
case.machine: Uniformation GK III Ultra (masked SLA / mSLA), CHITUBOX slicer, 3.6 s normal layer cure, lift 45 mm/min, retract 60 mm/min
case.orientation: Not stated for the cell axes. The 30 mm cubes were 'compressed along the build direction' in testing. The printer builds inverted (bottom-up mSLA). Each build held six specimens in two rows of three on the build plate.
case.outcome_words: "5-20 lattices did not produce open lattice structures. Although solid objects printed, the internal regions became homogeneous solids." Fig. 1a legend for 5-20: "Resin entrapment (solid)". Pilot: 2 mm cells "produced solid blocks owing to resin entrapment"
case.where: Sec. 2.2 (pilot 2 mm cells); Sec. 3.1 and Fig. 1a (printable window map, 5-20 = 'Resin entrapment (solid)') with Fig. 1b (resin-entrapment micrograph); Sec. 3.3 (5-10 and 5-15 degraded); Sec. 3.6 ('cells at or below 5 mm cannot be cleared of resin at high density'); Conclusions (a); SI Tables S5–S6 (5-20 shown as a dash, 'Dashes indicate print failures')
case.notes: The trapped material is uncured RESIN, not powder. The authors attribute it to 'a combination of light bleed/overcure into narrow pore channels and the inability to wash uncured resin out of the narrow channels'. The SI tables show 5-20 as a dash ('Dashes indicate print failures'), so no density or wall was measured. No wall thickness and no channel width is stated for 5-20. The paper gives only the first-order relation t ≈ ρL/3.09, and says the measured 5% walls came out 12–18% thinner than it. Washing was in IPA in an ultrasonic bath, then drying, then a 15 min UV post-cure (Creality UW-02, 365–385 nm). Specimens were 30 mm cubes (6 cells per edge at 5 mm). The 5-10 and 5-15 lattices printed (Fig. 1a: 'Successful print'), but the paper places them in a 'degraded-fidelity zone' (partial resin entrapment, cure broadening into the narrow channels, incomplete washing). Measured walls: 5-10 is 132 ± 3 µm in the main text and 131 ± 3 µm in SI Table S5; 5-15 is 236 ± 7 µm (SI Table S5). At matched wall thickness and with strength normalised by ρ², 5-10 reached only ≈46% of 10-5 and 5-15 ≈61% of 15-5. On raw UCS, 5-10 (0.43 ± 0.13 MPa) is above 10-5 (0.24 ± 0.04 MPa) (SI Table S6). Cells of 10, 15 and 20 mm printed over the full 5–20% range. Sec. 2.2 says 'A thin (200 µm) solid sheet was added to the top and bottom faces of the lattice CAD' to avoid resin penetration during sandwich-panel construction. The sentence comes right after the panel-core sentence and does not say whether the 30 mm compression cubes also had these skins. For the 2 mm pilot prints, the specimen size and settings are not stated separately. The authors say both window boundaries are 'specific to this resin–printer–exposure combination'. Preprint, not peer-reviewed.

kept.why: I read the published Springer PDF (CC BY 4.0; J. Mater. Res. 36(16), pp. 3182–3193). Springer blocks scripted downloads, so I took the copy from the Wayback Machine snapshot of the OA PDF. It is byte-identical (same SHA-256) to an earlier download, and its metadata carries the DOI. I rendered Table 1 (an image, p. 3183) and Fig. 7a (p. 3190). These are confirmed: p. 3189 says 'refresh rate of 50/50 on the laser sintering system EOSINT P395 ... layer thickness of 150 µm and the parameter set "Thinwall" ... 137 °C'. The cell types cube/FCCZ/dode/star come from 3-MATIC. The grid is 2.5/5/10/15 mm cells × 0.6/1.0/1.5/2.0 mm strut diameters, with each specimen made three times over the build space. The outcome quote on pp. 3183–3184 is exact. Corrections: (1) Table 1 shows the Cube results at 2.5 mm are not one outcome. The 0.6 mm strut is marked '-' (failure, the structure broke in post-processing). The 1.0 mm strut has a grey ✗ ('Powder not completly removable'). The 1.5 and 2.0 mm struts have a black ✗ ('enclosed volumes'). So wall_mm for the powder_trapped outcome is 1.0, 1.5, 2.0, and 0.6 mm belongs to a separate 'failed' case. (2) The case listed four cell types under kind 'cubic'. I restricted it to the Cube cell: Fig. 7a draws it with struts on the 12 cube edges only, so it is simple cubic, which settles the 'not verified' note. FCCZ, dodecahedron and star are kind 'other' and now appear in the notes only. (3) The notes now carry the Table 1 readings instead of 'Table 1 was not read'.

case.source_title: Mechanical characterization and numerical modeling of laser-sintered TPE lattice structures
case.authors_year: Kummert, Schmid, Risse, Kullmer (2021), J. Mater. Res. 36(16):3182–3193
case.material: EOS PrimePart ST (TPE-A, polyether block amide / PEBA), refresh rate 50/50
case.machine: EOSINT P395 (EOS), parameter set 'Thinwall', 137 °C process temperature
case.lattice_as_named: Cube (unit cell from Materialise 3-matic; Fig. 7a shows struts on the 12 cube edges only), built as cube-shaped 2 × 2 × 2-cell specimens
case.orientation: Not stated. Each 2 × 2 × 2-cell specimen was 'manufactured three times distributed over the build space'.
case.outcome_words: "regardless of the strut diameter a cell size of 2.5 mm cannot be produced, since actually free volumes remain sealed" (text). Table 1, Cube, 2.5 mm: 1.0 mm strut = "Powder not completly removable" [sic]; 1.5 and 2.0 mm = "enclosed volumes".
case.where: Results, 'Manufacturability of lattice structures using laser sintering': first paragraph (pp. 3183–3184) and Table 1, Cube rows, 2.5 mm column (p. 3183). Restated after Table 2 on p. 3184: 'regardless of the strut diameter and cell type, a cell size of 2.5 mm cannot be manufactured, since actually free volumes remain closed'. Material and methods, 'Design of lattice structures for laser sintering' (p. 3189); Fig. 7a (cell geometry, p. 3190).
case.notes: Table 1 (an image) was read from a rendered page. Legend: ✓ 'feasible', '-' 'failure', grey ✗ 'Powder not completly removable', black ✗ 'enclosed volumes'. Cube rows: at 2.5 mm, 0.6 '-', 1.0 grey ✗, 1.5 and 2.0 black ✗. At 5 mm, 0.6 '-', 1.0/1.5/2.0 ✓. At 10 and 15 mm, 0.6 '-', 1.0 '-', 1.5/2.0 ✓. The 0.6 mm strut at 2.5 mm is left out of this case because its outcome differs: the text says 'a strut thickness of 0.6 mm always leads to a failure of the structure already in the post-process'. FCCZ, dodecahedron and star (kind 'other') are also black ✗ 'enclosed volumes' at 2.5 mm for 1.0–2.0 mm struts. FCCZ at 5 mm: 1.0 ✓, 1.5 grey ✗, 2.0 black ✗. Dode and star need cells of 10 mm or more. Depowdering was unpacking plus 'free blasting (compressed air and glass beads)'. The source gives no volume fraction for the cube cell and no pore or channel width. Table 2's 'specific cell density' covers only dodecahedron cells at 10 and 15 mm (0.01–0.34). The text's threshold 'for a specific cell density of 0.9 and smaller, powder can be removed completely' does not fit Table 2's values, so it is ambiguous and possibly a typo. Sandwich cores (50 × 50 mm cover layers, DIN 53291): cubes with 1.5 mm struts at 15 mm cells failed early ('premature failure'). FCCZ 5 mm cells still kept powder ('The cover layers seem to make powder removal more difficult here'). The material is an elastomer powder; the paper notes that elastomeric powders 'show comparatively low flowability', which 'may lead to poor removability of the powder from the gaps'.

kept.why: I read the full preprint PDF (Research Square v1, CC BY 4.0) and the SI PDF, and rendered Fig. 1. Every field is found as given. Sec. 3.1 has the exact quote '5-5 lattices failed to print because the thin walls (nominally below ~130 µm) could not withstand the separation forces during layer lifting'. The same section gives the Stefan adhesion mechanism ('destroyed the object during printing') and 'should be read as a process parameter rather than a material constant'. Fig. 1a plots 5-5 as 'Thin-wall separation failure'. SI Tables S5 and S6 show 5-5 as a dash ('Dashes indicate print failures'), so no wall was measured. Sec. 3.2 gives the walls 132 ± 3 (10-5), 214 ± 10 (15-5) and 271 ± 11 µm (20-5). Sec. 3.3 says 5-10 and 10-5 'share the same measured wall thickness (132 ± 3 µm)'. Sec. 2.3 gives the 25 µm layer, GK III Ultra, 3.6 s cure and CHITUBOX. Sec. 2.5 says 'compressed along the build direction'. Conclusions (a) matches. Two inconsistencies sit inside the source and are not errors in the case. SI Table S5 lists the 5-10 wall as 131 ± 3 µm, not 132 ± 3. The text cites the pore micrograph as Fig. 1b, but the caption labels it 1c (1b is resin entrapment).

case.source_title: Partially decoupling cell size and density as tailorable design parameters in mSLA-printed gyroid cores for sustainable sandwich panels
case.authors_year: Luthuli, Schlesinger, Christodoulides, Vos, Gabriel, Dicks (2026, Research Square preprint v1)
case.material: eSun eResin-PLA Pro transparent (partially biobased PLA-based polyurethane acrylate photopolymer)
case.machine: Uniformation GK III Ultra (masked SLA / mSLA), CHITUBOX slicer, 3.6 s normal layer cure
case.wall_mm: nominally below ~0.13 (sheet; not measured because the print failed)
case.orientation: Not stated for the cell axes. The 30 mm cubes were tested along the build direction, and the printer builds inverted (bottom-up mSLA).
case.outcome_words: "5-5 lattices failed to print because the thin walls (nominally below ~130 µm) could not withstand the separation forces during layer lifting"
case.where: Sec. 3.1 and Fig. 1 (printable window, pore micrograph); Sec. 3.2 (measured walls); Conclusions (a)
case.notes: The stated mechanism is Stefan adhesion (peel suction) exceeding the strength of the incompletely cured lattice. Nearest successes in the same study: 10-5 printed with a measured wall of 132 ± 3 µm but with 'randomly distributed pores' in the walls; 15-5 had 214 ± 10 µm and 20-5 had 271 ± 11 µm. All 10, 15 and 20 mm cells printed at 5–20%. Since sheet thickness scales with density × cell size, 5-10 also had 132 ± 3 µm walls and printed. The authors say the ~130 µm threshold 'should be read as a process parameter rather than a material constant', shifting with exposure dose, vat-film adhesion and resin green strength. Preprint, not peer-reviewed.

kept.why: I read the full text and tables (Europe PMC PMC7924027, CC BY; Polymers 13(4):635, 2021). Sec. 2.1 and Table 3: unbranded PLA, Creality Ender 3, Cura 4.0, Bowden drive, 0.4 mm nozzle, 0.16 mm layer, 0.2 mm extrusion width, 200/50 °C, 60 mm/s, no support, raft. The Up mini 2 (direct drive) settings are 0.15 mm layer and 0.3 mm width, listed under ABS. Table 4, CVC 'Cube vertex centroid': block 31/31/31 mm, strut diameter '0.70 *', strut length 4, overhang 45, cell size 5, contravened guideline 4. The row is aligned correctly; I checked the XML colspans. Table 5: CVC is PLA 'VP' and ABS 'A'. Sec. 3.2 says 'structures CVC, HPV, TOV and HPD could not be printed (Figure 2)', and the quoted outcome sentence is verbatim. Sec. 4.1 says 'It was not possible to print miniature lattices CVC, TOV, HPV, and HPD in the Ender 3 printer using PLA filament, on a 1:1 scale'. It also gives a nominal 0.7 mm strut against an effective 0.89 mm in ABS and 0.75 mm in PLA, and contains the 'long inclined struts (4 mm or longer in CVC and HPV)', 'vertical struts with a length over 0.5 mm' and 'overhang angles over 65° and a length over 2 mm' quotes, the 2:1 strut of 1.4 mm, and CVC printed in PLA and PC on the Up mini 2 (Fig. 15). Fig. 11 caption: 0.89 ± 0.06 mm. Table 6: CVC 'A, minor stringing' and HPD 'F', while the text and the Fig. 4 caption say HPV failed. Sec. 2.2: 'Specimens were tested in the same orientation of printing.' No volume fraction is given for PLA; Table 7 has only ABS densities in g/cm3, so the empty field is right. Every field and note matches. One small point: the Up mini 2 parameters in Table 3 are for the ABS runs, and the settings for the PLA and PC runs on that printer are not stated.

I read the full text (Europe PMC PMC12567854; Polymers 17(20):2804, 2025) and viewed Figs. 8–11. These are as stated: Sec. 2 'closed BCC lattice structures enclosed by solid walls with defined vent openings', '2–5 layers in the z-direction', sandblasting at 4.4 bar from 400 mm for a constant duration, and X-ray checks. Sec. 4: 'the BCC unit cell used in this study had an edge length of 5 mm'. Table 1 gives rod 2.66 → 0.39 and 3 → 0.47, and 1 → 0.07. All of Table 2's depths match. Both outcome quotes are verbatim (abstract; Sec. 4 for ρ 0.39). No print layer thickness is stated. Three corrections: (1) kind changes from bcc to other. The Fig. 8 CAD cell has square-section bars on all 12 cube edges plus four round body diagonals, and the tiled specimen in Fig. 8 keeps that edge grid. That makes it BCC plus cube edges, the same treatment as the Parodo cuboidal BCC case. (2) The HP MJF 4200 and PA12 are named for the 45 accuracy specimens (abstract, Sec. 2). For the lattices the paper only mentions 'depowdering guidelines for PA12 MJF parts' and does not restate the machine. (3) The new notes warn that the stated 5 mm cell, the 1–3 mm rods and ρ 0.07–0.47 do not agree. My own check computation shows that Table 1 matches a 10 mm cell of this shape, not a 5 mm one. The mm values should not be used for a wall or channel rule check until this is resolved.

case.source_title: Accuracy and Powder Removal Limits in Multi Jet Fusion 3D Printing
case.material: PA12 (grade not stated; named for the accuracy specimens in the abstract and in the Sec. 4 depowdering discussion, not restated for the lattice specimens)
case.machine: HP MJF 4200 (named for the accuracy specimens in Sec. 2; not restated for the lattice specimens)
case.lattice_as_named: closed BCC lattice enclosed by solid walls with defined vent openings (Fig. 8 cell: four round body diagonals plus square-section cube-edge bars)
case.wall_mm: 2.66 and 3.0 (rod diameter of the round struts; size of the cube-edge bars not stated); 1.0–3.0 tested
case.orientation: Not stated for the lattice blocks. Block thickness is counted as 2–5 cell layers 'in the z-direction' (Sec. 2). The X-ray images (Figs. 10–11) show the cleaned zone growing from the stepped face of the stepped specimen (Fig. 8: sections 5, 4, 3 and 2 cells high). The text does not state where the vents are.
case.outcome_words: "high-density structures (ρ = 0.39–0.47) were limited to only 1.5–1.7 layers"; for ρ 0.39: "it was not possible to achieve sandblasting of more than 1.6 layers"
case.where: Abstract; Sec. 2; Sec. 4 (Fig. 8 cell and specimen CAD, Table 1 rod vs ρ, Table 2 cleaned depth, Figs. 10–12); Sec. 5; Conclusions
case.notes: The authors call it BCC, but the CAD cell in Fig. 8 (left) is a cube frame of square-section edge bars with four round body diagonals, and the tiled specimen (Fig. 8, right) keeps the edge grid. So the kind is 'other' (BCC plus cube edges), as in the Parodo cuboidal BCC case. CAUTION: the stated cell (5 mm), rod diameters (1–3 mm) and relative densities (0.07–0.47) do not agree with each other. The following is our own check computation, not a value from the paper. For the Fig. 8 cell shape, a 5 mm cell would be about 0.24 solid with 1 mm rods and about 0.96 with 3 mm rods; a plain 5 mm BCC with 1 mm rods is about 0.18. A 10 mm cell reproduces Table 1 to within about 0.02 (0.07 / 0.24 / 0.39 / 0.47 at 1 / 2 / 2.66 / 3 mm). So either the cell is about 10 mm or the rods are half the stated size. Do not use the mm values for a wall or channel rule check until this is resolved; the relative densities and the layer counts are the usable part. Depowdering was automated sandblasting at 4.4 bar from 400 mm for a constant time, checked visually and by industrial X-ray. Vent size and position, blasting duration and print layer thickness are not stated. Table 2 gives the cleaned depth in cell layers for each relative density (rod mm): 0.07 (1.00) → 5.00, the whole block, 'the powder was removed entirely'; 0.11 (1.33) → 3.00; 0.18 (1.66) → 2.67; 0.24 (2.00) → 2.33; 0.31 (2.33) → 2.00; 0.39 (2.66) → 1.67; 0.47 (3.00) → 1.50. The text gives about 2.6 and 1.6 for ρ 0.18 and 0.39. Blocks 2 layers thick were cleaned completely at ρ 0.18 and 0.39. The result depends on depth: whether powder escapes depends on how many cells lie between it and the opening, as well as on density. The HP MJF 4200 and PA12 are named only for the accuracy part of the study.

kept.why: I read the full text (Europe PMC PMC11990384; Materials 18(7):1679, 2025) and viewed Figs. 3–5. Sec. 2.1 and Table 1: Stratasys F190 CR with manufacturer-fixed settings ('not adjustable by the user'), chamber 75 °C, nozzle 0.400 mm, slicing height 0.127 mm. The nozzle temperatures (ABS 190 °C, support 265 °C) are listed there too but are not in the case. ABS filament is 1.75 mm. QSR soluble support was printed at maximum fill density and dissolved in a water and NaOH-based solution (Sec. 2.1, 3.1). Table 2: L5_Dr5 0.4 mm, L5_Dr10 0.6 mm and L5_Dr15 0.8 mm at M = 5/10/15 %; L10_Dr5 0.8 mm; L15_Dr15 1.9 mm; struts of the built cells range 0.8–3.0 mm. The Sec. 3.1 quote is verbatim, followed by 'Consequently, all 5 mm cells were excluded'. Fig. 3 caption: 'Damaged 5 mm lattice cell specimen (M = 10%, left; M = 15%, right)'. The photo shows single cube-frame cells with BCC diagonals, one with its vertical edges missing. This confirms single cells with cube-edge struts, so kind 'other' is right. Sec. 2 defines x/y struts 'parallel to the printing orientation', z struts 'orthogonal to the printing orientation' and s struts 'inclined'. The case paraphrases this as the printing plane with z vertical, which matches the layer lines visible in Fig. 5b. The Fig. 5a caption quote is verbatim, and Sec. 3.2.1 gives the 0.6–1.8 % edge deviation. One inconsistency in the source does not affect the key fields: L15_Dr15 is 1.9 mm in Table 2 but 2.2 mm in Table 3. Table 3 also gives a measured mean strut of 0.72 ± 0.14 mm for L10_Dr5.
